context:
Follow the established pattern used for table_mode: attribute on adapter
base class, set in runner, read in DataLoader/DataSourceResolver.

The key insight is that PLATFORM_FORMAT_PREFERENCES is already correctly
configured for all platforms. The fix is making it the actual default instead
of a fallback behind manifest format_preference.
description:
The manifest's format_preference field (persisted by previous --table-format
conversion runs) takes priority over platform default preferences. This means
if a user previously ran --table-format delta, ALL subsequent runs silently
use delta format even without --table-format.

Concrete failure: TPC-H SF1 on DuckDB fails because the existing manifest has
format_preference: ["delta", "parquet", "iceberg", "tbl"] from a prior
conversion. Delta entries are directories (is_directory: True), which the shard
loader can't handle via the generic file path. Same root cause for
read_primitives, write_primitives, and transaction_primitives (all share
TPC-H SF1 data).

Principle: BenchBox users should NEVER be surprised by the data format used
for loading. Platform preferences should always drive default format selection.
PLATFORM_FORMAT_PREFERENCES is already correctly configured (tbl first for
SQL platforms, delta first for lakehouse platforms) - it's just not being used
as the default.

Two orthogonal changes:
1. Always prefer platform defaults in native mode (one-line change)
2. Thread explicit --table-format to DataSourceResolver so explicit user
   requests still override platform defaults for that run

anti_patterns.dont: add directory-globbing hacks to the shard loader
anti_patterns.why: yesterday's failed approach tried to load delta parquet parts without delta metadata, which is semantically wrong

anti_patterns.dont: change manifest format_preference to always be ['tbl', ...]
anti_patterns.why: lakehouse platforms (Databricks, Trino) legitimately default to delta/iceberg via their platform preferences

anti_patterns.dont: modify the conversion pipeline's manifest update logic
anti_patterns.why: it correctly records what was converted, it just shouldn't drive default selection

anti_patterns.dont: remove delta/iceberg/parquet from DuckDB's supported formats
anti_patterns.why: the platform genuinely supports them when explicitly requested

preserves.behavior: --table-format CLI flag still works: explicit format requests override platform defaults for that run
All 15 benchmarks that currently pass at SF1 on DuckDB continue to pass
Conversion pipeline still updates manifest format_preference (conversion.py:236-239) - it just no longer drives default selection
External table mode (table_mode='external') still uses manifest preference order (not platform defaults)
PLATFORM_FORMAT_PREFERENCES table in format_capabilities.py - this is the source of truth for default format ordering per platform
